exposure: confidence in knowledge of pregnancy and birth
outcome: preference for prenatal care provider type
cohort: The study included 782 women aged 18-35 who had never been pregnant but desired to have at least one child in the future.
finding: Confidence in knowledge of pregnancy and birth was related to lower fear of childbirth and a preference for midwives over obstetricians as prenatal care providers.
mod_finding: Confidence in knowledge was not associated with a preference for cesarean birth.
cross-section timing: Performed on nulliparous women before pregnancy
